content:
Hi everyone,

I am organizing a project with participants from the MadLean meetup in Madrid (#Geographic locality > Madrid, Spain). Last meetup, we voted to start a project together formalizing some material on left-orderable groups, corresponding to Chapter 1 of my PhD thesis:
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.07035.

From a quick look at mathlib4, I could not find an explicit definition such as IsLeftOrderable, nor a formalization of positive cones. I did find formalization related to the zero-divisor conjecture.

Our tentative goal would be to:
• introduce the basic definitions (IsLeftOrderable, positive cones, etc.),
• construct some explicit examples of left-orderable groups,
• formalize the dynamical characterization of left orders.

The current participants include myself, two faculty members at UCM (math/CS), graduate students in formal methods, and software engineers with strong functional programming and mathematics backgrounds. The goal would be to initiate them to contributing to mathlib.

Before we start, I wanted to ask whether this seems like a useful and realistic project given the current state of mathlib. The participants could get their first project experience by proving the statements, while I would to draft the definitions and statements, and discuss the design on Zulip.

Any advice on scope, naming conventions, or existing work I may have missed would be very helpful.

(edited because I apparently forgot what I already got in to Mathlib!)
Positive cones in groups and rings are available in Mathlib under docs#GroupCone and docs#RingCone. Note that they are pointed, unlike the definition in your thesis.

I am refactoring this formalisation to unify the two definitions, defining instead a prediate IsPointed on Submonoid. #33942 is the first PR in this direction.
But yes, the existing material on ordered groups assumes commutativity, and you do not. eg docs#IsOrderedMonoid
Non-commutative ordered groups are covered in mathlib using docs#MulLeftMono

In case it is helpful, I have a project where I formalized some theorems about non-commutative ordered groups and semigroups here: https://ericluap.com/OrderedSemigroups/
(For example, it has that every left linear ordered group is monoid-order-isomorphic to a subgroup of the real numbers.)

Made PR #41505 proposing a definition for IsLeftOrderable using Claude Fable with the help of @Yaël Dillies.

(Thank you so much again for the help! :folded_hands: )
